lastCommit.message:
OTA-1881 — the Crucible keeps its hooks

The owner tapped FUSE in asgardar and the game broke. On a Pixel 10 Pro XL,
Android 17, release 2026-09-24-1880, at 20:36:11.483Z, the screen went to
SOMETHING BROKE carrying React's own sentence:

    Rendered more hooks than during the previous render.
        at FusionPickerModal

The error boundary caught it, so the process survived and the ledger calls it a
"screen crash (recovered)" — but the Crucible never opened.

THE CAUSE WAS TOPOLOGY, AND IT WAS UNCONDITIONAL. FusionPickerModal stays MOUNTED
while shut and renders null through `if (!visible) return null`. Three hooks — a
useRef and the two `pres` useEffects — sat BELOW that line, so a closed render ran
15 hooks and an open one ran 18. The extra three arrive on the very render where
`visible` flips, which is the render the FUSE tap causes. This was not a race and
not a device: every opening of this card broke the rule, and Android is only where
it was caught. (My own brief to myself said 6 above the return and 2 below; the
measured truth is 15 and 3, because a generic-typed `useMemo<…>(` or `useState<…>(`
does not match a naive `use[A-Z]\w*\(` scan. Count them with the generics.)

THE REPAIR IS THE HOOKS MOVING, AND NOTHING ELSE. All three were lifted above the
guard and their bodies keyed to `visible`, which reproduces their old behaviour
honestly: living below a conditional return, they behaved as though they mounted
when the card opened and unmounted when it shut, and that is exactly what their
react-mount / react-unmount rows mean. Keyed to `visible`, the pair still brackets
the span the card is actually on screen, the stage ref still clears while shut so
the next opening announces its stage, and nothing writes a diagnostic row while
the surface is down. No fusion rule, permit, cost, navigation or OTA-1875
responder topology moved.

  app/components/FusionPickerModal.tsx   three hooks above the guard, keyed to
                                         `visible`; guard still a plain early
                                         return at line 221

AND NOTHING HERE IS PLATFORM-SHAPED. A hook-ordering rule that held on one
platform and not another would not be a rule. There is no device, OS or version
test in this repair, and §C fails if one ever appears — it reads the file with
comments STRIPPED first, because the unstripped census failed on my own comment
naming the device, which is the OTA-1721 class: an instrument acting on a comment
that names what it hunts for.

THE SUITE COUNTS RENDERS, NOT STRINGS. A regex would have been satisfied by moving
the lines and would say nothing about whether React accepts the result, so every
case drives the real component through real `visible` transitions and fails if
React throws — which is what the owner saw.

  ota1881TheCrucibleKeepsItsHooks   15/15 — the four crash transitions incl. the
                                    exact mounted-shut-then-opened FUSE case; no
                                    hook below the guard; no device branch and no
                                    suppression; the presentation rows still
                                    bracket the open card; card contents,
                                    transaction path, OTA-1875 topology and zero
                                    resource spend
  related contracts                 ota1875, ota1878, ota1880 + this suite:
                                    4 suites, 81/81
  fast surface                      1380/1380 suites · 16,122 passed · 3 skipped
  typecheck:ci                      exit 0
  typecheck:tests                   OK — at baseline (196), no growth
  lint                              clean
  check gates                       22/22

ONE NEGATIVE CONTROL, not committed, production restored byte-identically (md5
618988f3d000037e905a054cb19cb303 before and after). Putting ONE of the three hooks
back below the guard turns 9 of 15 red and reproduces React's exact sentence at
the moved line.

TWO HARNESS FACTS, both mine, both worth the next reader's time. Teardown must
flush inside act(): React defers a passive effect's destroy past unmount(), so an
unwrapped afterEach let this card's own react-unmount row land during the NEXT
test's mount and be counted against it — the row was right, only its timing was
the harness's fault. And NO `{ virtual: true }` on a module that genuinely exists:
a virtual mock on the real onnxruntime held only while this suite ran ALONE, and in
a shared run the real binding loaded and died on "Cannot read properties of
undefined (reading 'install')" — failing a NEIGHBOUR suite, not this one. OTA-1246
already wrote that lesson down; matching its house pattern is what survives a
whole-suite run.

#206 — the earlier Fusing-Crucible investigation closed as INSUFFICIENT EVIDENCE.
That was the right disposition for the evidence it had: the surface emitted no
`pres` row and nothing named a mechanism. It did not know this mechanism. This
crash supplied it.

SEPARATE / UNRESOLVED NON-BLOCKING OBSERVATION. 13.45s after the render throw the
process died with no signal while the in-flight marker still read action "fuse".
Nothing in this evidence proves the throw caused that death: the same no-signal
shape appears twice earlier in the same ledger under unrelated taps ("missions",
"LORE"), memory warnings were none, heap ran 12->28MB, the native queue was idle
at 0 jobs past 3s and there were 0 model contexts. The shared word "fuse" is a
stale in-flight marker, not a causal link. Not closed here, and not widened here.

NOT CLAIMED: physical verification on the owner's hardware.
